text:
sasha: Heads-up — experimenting with rotating prompt fingerprints + bucketized request_id to reduce cardinality in traces. Thoughts on a schema so dashboards and rollouts keep working?

nate: Quick q — rotation scope? per-customer salt, global, or per-region? Need to understand migration implications.

kelly: Per-customer salt + explicit salt version attribute is my vote. Put a small `salt_version` on spans so Console can group/coalesce. e.g. `telemetry_salt_v=3`. :thumbsup:

ajay: We must keep fingerprints stable for retries and within the same request. Implementation idea: `prompt_fp = truncate(hex(sha256(hmac(salt, prompt))), 12)` and separately emit `user_bucket = hash(user_id) % 1024` so we can aggregate without exposing raw ids.

sasha: Proposed attribute set: `prompt_fp` (12 hex chars), `telemetry_salt_v`, `req_bucket` (0..1023), and `pii_scrubbed=true` when prompt is removed. Also include `prompt_source` (template|freeform) for better evals.

nate: Exporter path: OTLP -> collector -> internal exporter. Collector should perform hmac using customer key before we ever persist. We also need a plan for salt rotation: dashboards need a way to map old->new (migration job or coalescing view).

kelly: Retention policy idea: keep raw mapping only 7–14 days, keep aggregated metrics (counts per prompt_fp) for 1 year. Important: do not store raw prompts or reversible hashes. HMAC with per-customer key + truncation mitigates brute-force.

ajay: Note on perf: HMAC per-span is cheap but avoid slow KDFs in the hot path. Do HMAC in collector in a fast C implementation or use a native processor. Also ensure deterministic seed for `req_bucket` so retries map to same bucket: `req_bucket = xxhash64(request_id + salt) % 1024`.

sasha: small example collector config we can iterate on:

```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch: {}
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: prompt
        action: delete
      - key: prompt_fp
        action: insert
        value: "{{hmac_sha256(prompt, env:COLLECTOR_SALT)}}"
exporters:
  internal/otel:
    endpoint: "internal-otel:4317"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [internal/otel]
```

devops-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary deploy of collector with attr-processor to `canary` namespace (release: telemetry-salt-v3). Link: https://deploys.internal/release/telemetry-salt-v3 :robot_face:

kelly: Console UX: show salt_version in the span list, provide a "coalesce" toggle to join multiple salt versions for metric charts, and an admin migration page that runs equivalence scoring for high-volume prompt_fps. Also we need a signal in Optimize to detect quality regressions when salt changes.

nate: I can own the Console join UX. Opening INF-3892 to track: console coalesce + migration helper.

sasha: Action items: 1) PR collector attribute processor (ajay), 2) docs for SDKs to emit `request_id` and `prompt_source` (sasha), 3) console coalesce UX (nate). Canary window = 48h, then gradual ramp.

kelly: One last thought — telemetry exporters should redact any leftover `prompt` attr if present and emit a warning metric so we catch instrumentation gaps.

ajay: Agreed. I'll add an exporter-level guard that rejects traces with `prompt` unless `pii_scrubbed=true`.

sasha: Nice. Thanks all — we should be able to cut cardinality ~10-100x if adopters set `req_bucket` and we do sensible salt rotation. :rocket:
